- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise sharply, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If supply net is heavily negative (e.g., -10+), model should not over-forecast recovery; adjust downward bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After a strong bullish sentiment spike, model should not assume continuation; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5–7 day average.
- If official events show high bearish pressure (e.g., bearish > 30), model must reduce forecast slope and shift toward lower end of 30d range.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model should avoid linear extrapolation; use weighted average of recent 3–5 day mean.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, apply downward correction of 3–5% to avoid overconfidence in short-term rebound.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model should not assume continuation; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 3–5 days after peak.
